events.title: Thomas Paine publishes Common Sense
events.description: In Philadelphia, Thomas Paine anonymously published the pamphlet Common Sense. It made a plain-spoken case for American independence from Britain and against hereditary monarchy.
events.significance: It sold in huge numbers and helped turn colonial opinion toward independence months before the Declaration of Independence.

events.title: The London Underground opens
events.description: The Metropolitan Railway opened in London, running between Paddington and Farringdon. It was the world's first underground passenger railway. Its steam trains left the tunnels filled with smoke.
events.significance: It launched urban rapid transit. Subway systems around the world followed its model.

events.title: Spindletop gusher launches the Texas oil boom
events.description: Near Beaumont, Texas, the Lucas well at Spindletop Hill blew in with a huge column of oil. It produced far more than any U.S. well before it.
events.significance: It opened the modern American petroleum era and helped make oil a central fuel of the 20th-century economy.

events.title: The United Nations General Assembly holds its first meeting
events.description: Delegates from 51 nations gathered in London for the first session of the UN General Assembly. They met only months after the end of World War II.
events.significance: It marked the start of the UN's work as a forum for international cooperation and conflict prevention.
